findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Quote or inline the original plan's complete scope list (or a definitive enumeration of its top-level deliverables) in AC1 so that 'nothing orphaned' is verifiable by diff rather than by reading prose.
evidence: 'between them cover the whole original scope: the relocation (S1) and the 429 policy (S2), with nothing from the original plan orphaned'

The plan enumerates two parts (relocation, 429 policy) in the body, but the original full plan text is not quoted; an executor verifying AC1 must infer completeness from the summary prose rather than a canonical checklist.
findings.finding: AC1 asks an executor to verify 'nothing from the original plan orphaned', but the 'original plan' (the pre-split version of this ticket) is neither quoted in full nor linked to a persistent artifact. An executor must reconstruct what 'the whole original scope' was by reading the prose in the Context section, making the completeness check judgment-dependent rather than deterministic.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — first bullet: 'both children exist…with nothing from the original plan orphaned'
scenarios: An executor checks AC1: they confirm S1 and S2 exist and cover relocation + 429 policy, but cannot determine whether the original plan contained a third concern (e.g., observability hooks, metric emission) that was silently dropped in the split.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'with nothing from the original plan orphaned' with an explicit enumeration: e.g., 'S1 covers (a) moving the retry/error cluster out of transport.py; S2 covers (b) adding Retry-After-aware 429 handling; no other deliverable existed in the pre-split plan.' This makes AC1 mechanically checkable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an ADR or AGENTS.md entry capturing (a) the new _errors module boundary, (b) the per-call opt-in contract for 429 retries, and (c) the constraint that 429 retry must not reach mutation sites — so the finding is in living documentation, not only in ticket comments.
evidence: "A pure, behaviour-preserving relocation" — no doc update mentioned for S1
"scopes the retry to IDEMPOTENT READS behind a per-call opt-in defaulting to OFF" — a new caller contract with no AGENTS.md or ADR update called for
"The constraint that shapes S2, restated here because it is the one that must not be lost in the split" — this concern is parked in ticket comments, not in living documentation
Neither child plan nor the parent plan references any AGENTS.md / ADR / design-doc update task
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel architectural decision — extracting the retry/error cluster from transport.py into a new _errors module and establishing a per-call opt-in contract for 429 retries — but does not call for any update to AGENTS.md, an ADR, or a design doc. The split creates a new module boundary, a new caller contract (opt-in flag), and a constraint about mutation sites that future contributors must discover from ticket comments rather than from living documentation.
findings.location: Approach section — "S1: extract the retry/error cluster out of transport.py" and "S2: add the 429 policy in the extracted module"
scenarios: A contributor unfamiliar with the ticket history adds a retry at _with_connection_retry without knowing the mutation-site constraint, re-introducing the duplicate-issue defect — because the constraint lives only in ticket comments, not in AGENTS.md or an ADR that would appear in normal code review.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a task in S1 or S2 (whichever closes last) to update AGENTS.md with a short note: the _errors module owns retry/backoff policy; callers must set opt_in_429_retry=True explicitly; mutation call sites (create_issue and peers) must never set this flag.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add at least one acceptance criterion that carries a concrete, user-observable validation mechanism — e.g., 'S2's test suite includes an integration or contract test demonstrating that a simulated 429 response triggers a retry and the operation ultimately succeeds, rather than propagating a hard failure' — so that closing this parent ticket implies the customer problem is demonstrably fixed, not merely that coordination tasks completed.
evidence: All five ACs are structural/process checks: children exist, link recorded, constraint documented in S2, history preserved, children closed.
No AC reads like 'on a rate-limited DC instance, a rebar operation that would have 429'd now retries and succeeds' or equivalent.
Rubric F4(d): 'at least one criterion carries a concrete validation mechanism (before/after workflow comparison, an operational metric target, dogfooding).'
findings.finding: None of the five acceptance criteria in this parent/coordination ticket carries a concrete validation mechanism that confirms the user-facing problem is actually solved; the closest AC is 'both children are CLOSED before this ticket closes,' which is a process gate, not a before/after or operational signal confirming that 429 responses on a DC instance now result in successful retries rather than hard failures.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria section (all five bullet points)
scenarios: A reviewer closing this parent ticket can verify all five ACs without ever confirming that a real or synthetic rate-limited DC instance actually works end-to-end.
The children could both close with unit tests only and no integration signal; this ticket would pass its own ACs while the customer problem remains unvalidated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC such as: '- [ ] S2 carries at least one test (integration, contract, or parametrised unit) that simulates a DC 429 response on an IDEMPOTENT read call and asserts the operation succeeds after retry, providing an observable before/after signal for the customer-facing fix.'

findings.finding: S2's acceptance criteria hardcode transport.py line numbers from the pre-S1 state of the file (`:455`, `:469`, `:567` for the three _paged_search callers; `:421` for `_call_logged`). S1 removes lines from transport.py by moving the six-member cluster to retry.py. Even accounting for re-export lines added back, the net removal will shift every subsequent line number. The cited lines will not point to the claimed locations after S1 lands, making S2's per-call-site assertions unverifiable as written.
findings.location: child 6758-26b8-c9ea-4c5d, Acceptance criteria (the _paged_search AC) and Approach section ('_call_logged … defined at transport.py:421')
findings.suggested_fix: Replace all transport.py:NNN citations in S2 with symbol-anchored references (function name + call context) rather than line numbers, so the AC remains verifiable regardless of how many lines S1's relocation adds or removes from transport.py.

findings.finding: S2's Scope section names only `retry.py` as a modified file, but the opt-in parameter must also be threaded through `_call_logged` (transport.py:271) and added to every opted-in call site in `transport.py` — including the direct `_with_connection_retry` calls at probe_remote (:493), get_comment_map's inner per-issue loop (:473), and transition_issue_by_name's read leg (:373). These are mandatory `transport.py` edits that S2's scope omits entirely, leaving an owned-by-none gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `transport.py` to S2's Scope section. Enumerate the specific lines requiring opt-in edits: _call_logged (:271, to forward the flag), get_comment_map's inner loop (:473, direct call), probe_remote (:493, direct call), and transition_issue_by_name's read leg (:373, direct call).
